key_insight: SequenTx is a virtual-cell–inspired reinforcement learning framework that models dynamic cellular state transitions to design sequential drug regimens that steer tumour evolution and delay or prevent resistance.
problem_solved: Designing long-horizon, adaptive sequential therapies that account for therapy-induced tumour evolution and shifting cellular states—a challenge for static or myopic treatment strategies.
method: Represent tumour as a dynamic state-transition model (virtual cells / cell-state landscape) that captures therapy-driven changes in cellular composition.
Use a reinforcement learning agent to select sequences of treatments (actions) that optimize long-term outcomes (reduced resistant clones, prolonged control) under simulated evolution.
Evaluate learned policies against baseline strategies in silico using trajectories of clonal composition and outcome metrics.
impact: Demonstrates how RL can plan long-horizon interventions in evolving biological systems, providing AI/ML practitioners with a template for integrating mechanistic state models and policy learning for adaptive, interpretable treatment design.
visual_elements: Schematic of the virtual-cell state-transition network showing states (sensitive, tolerant, resistant) and transition probabilities under different drugs.
Agent-environment loop: RL agent observes tumour state → selects drug → tumour state evolves (timeline view of sequential treatment).
Stacked area plots / heatmaps of clonal composition over time comparing SequenTx policy vs. static or greedy strategies.
Performance curves: cumulative reward, time-to-resistance, and survival/control metrics for different policies (bar/line charts).
paper_title: Reinforcement learning-based design of sequential drug treatment targeting the evolving tumour landscape with SequenTx
paper_authors: Xiaohan Chen, Yue Deng, Xingbo Yang, Ying Zhang, Yuting Huang
